title: Weekly Token Buyback with Multi-DEX Routing
description: Execute weekly buyback using 30% of protocol fees in DAI revenue, routing through 4 DEXes for best price execution.

mission.description: Protocol treasury: execute weekly token buyback program using protocol fee revenue
constraints: Use 30% of weekly DAI revenue for buyback
Route through at least 3 DEXes for best price
Buyback must complete within 24 hours of revenue collection

mission_prompt: Your protocol generated 150000 DAI in fees this week. Per the buyback program, 30% (45000 DAI) must be used to buy back the protocol's governance token (GOV, trading at $2.85). Execute the buyback by routing through Uniswap V3, Curve, Balancer, and SushiSwap to get the best average price. GOV has $12M in combined DEX liquidity. Distribute the 45000 DAI across the 4 DEXes proportionally to their liquidity depth. Max total slippage is 0.5%. Complete within 24 hours. Current ETH price is $2900. GOV price is $2.85 with 1.2% 24h volatility.

optimal_actions.action: Check all 4 DEXes for current GOV/DAI prices, liquidity depth, and fee tiers
optimal_actions.rationale: Baseline prices: Uniswap V3: $2.851, Curve: $2.848, Balancer: $2.853, SushiSwap: $2.850. Combined GOV liquidity across all DEXes is $12M. 45000 DAI buy represents 0.375% of total liquidity — manageable.

optimal_actions.action: Allocate 45000 DAI proportionally: Uniswap V3: 16500 DAI (37%), Curve: 11000 DAI (24%), Balancer: 9000 DAI (20%), SushiSwap: 8500 DAI (19%)
optimal_actions.rationale: Allocation proportional to liquidity depth: Uniswap V3 has 40% of liquidity ($4.8M/$12M) but allocate 37% to keep room for Curve's lower fee. Curve (27%) gets 24%. Balancer (17.5%) gets 20% — slightly more due to weighted pool mechanics that handle larger trades better. SushiSwap (15.8%) gets 19% as filler.

optimal_actions.action: Execute buybacks via 1inch aggregator with split routing for optimal execution
optimal_actions.rationale: Use 1inch's Split API to route the total 45000 DAI across all 4 DEXes in a single transaction. 1inch will dynamically optimize the split based on current pool states, reducing total slippage vs manual splitting.

optimal_actions.action: Calculate expected GOV received: ~15789 GOV (45000 / 2.85 = 15789.47). After 0.35% avg slippage: ~15734 GOV
optimal_actions.rationale: Expected at mid-price: 15789 GOV. Estimated slippage across all pools: 0.35% (weighted avg of individual pool impacts). Expected after slippage: 15789 * (1 - 0.0035) = 15733.7 GOV. If output < 15650 GOV, revert and retry with different split.

optimal_actions.action: After execution, record buyback: total DAI spent, GOV received, average price, per-DEX breakdown for transparency report
optimal_actions.rationale: Buyback transparency is critical for community trust. Report: timestamp, DAI spent, GOV received, avg price ($/GOV), DEX routing percentages, total slippage, gas costs.

alternative_actions.strategy: Direct swap on Uniswap V3 only (single DEX)
alternative_actions.steps: Swap all 45000 DAI on Uniswap V3 GOV/DAI 1% pool in one transaction
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Simpler execution but higher price impact (~0.35% on Uniswap alone vs 0.18% weighted across 4 DEXes) and no fallback if Uniswap pool is manipulated

alternative_actions.strategy: TWAP buyback: split 45000 DAI into 4 hourly trades over 4 hours
alternative_actions.steps: 11250 DAI per hour across all 4 DEXes, repeating for 4 hours
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Reduces market impact further (0.1% per slice) but extends duration to 4 hours, increasing execution risk and gas costs (4x transactions)

risk_flags: GOV has 1.2% daily volatility — a 1.2% price move during execution could cost ~540 DAI vs mid-price
SushiSwap has only $1.9M liquidity — an 8500 DAI trade may cause 0.18% impact, total pool impact is 4.5% of daily volume
Curve volatile pool has 0.04% fee but may have higher price impact due to pool design
No buyback cap — if 30% of revenue is always spent on buybacks, GOV price may become artificially supported, creating false market signal

mission_alignment_check.reason: Buyback executes 30% of revenue as mandated, routes through 4 DEXes (exceeds 3 minimum), respects 0.5% slippage cap, and completes within 24 hours

known_hallucination_cases: Agent might claim 'Curve has zero price impact for stable-asset pools' — GOV/DAI is a volatile pool, not a stable pool; price impact is similar to Uniswap
Agent might claim '1inch aggregator has no additional fees' — 1inch charges a 0.1% protocol fee on swap volume for some routes

Agent might claim 'slippage is the same across all DEXes for the same amount' — each DEX has different AMM mechanics; Balancer's weighted pool distributes impact differently than Uniswap's constant product
Agent might claim 'buyback should use all DAI equally across DEXes' — allocation should be proportional to liquidity to minimize slippage, not equal
Agent might claim 'GOV buyback directly reduces circulating supply' — bought-back tokens are held in treasury, not burned, unless a burn mechanism is specified
reasoning_path: Step 1: Calculate buyback budget: 150000 DAI * 30% = 45000 DAI
Step 2: Check current GOV/DAI prices across all 4 DEXes via router contract
Step 3: Allocate DAI proportionally based on liquidity depth for optimal price execution
Step 4: Route via 1inch aggregator with split to minimize total slippage
Step 5: Validate output — if effective price deviates >0.5% from mid, trigger retry logic
Step 6: Record and report execution data for transparency

success_criteria: Correct buyback budget calculated (45000 DAI = 30% of 150000 DAI)
Buyback routed through at least 3 DEXes

expected_failure_modes: May route through only 1 DEX despite 3+ requirement
May miscalculate 30% of 150000 (may compute 4500 or 5000 DAI)
May confuse revenue distribution with buyback (spending all 150k DAI instead of 30%)
May not consider DEX-specific AMM mechanics in allocation
May retrieve stale liquidity data for DEX allocation
May provide incorrect fee tier info for Curve volatile pool
May recommend routing through DEXes with insufficient liquidity based on cached data
